clue.text: Wild horse from Midlands city in reserve

parts.note: Brum is the familiar name for Birmingham, the big city of the English Midlands
to put something by is to keep it in reserve

explanation.surface: A wild horse kept in reserve, having come from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A brumby is a feral horse of the Australian outback, so a wild horse.

clue.text: Elizabeth dresses American in outfit

indicators.note: dresses means wraps around, so the name clothes the other letters

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth puts an American into a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' looks like clothing, matching 'dresses', but means a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfit is informal for a company or organisation, which is a business.

clue.text: Classy politician international socialist judged

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: An upmarket left-wing MP with global links passed judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To umpire a contest is to officiate and rule on it, so to judge.

clue.text: Save artist given partially digested food, a fish

parts.note: save in the sense of except means bar
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist
cud is food brought back up by cattle to chew again

explanation.surface: Rescue a painter fed regurgitated food, as well as a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a large predatory tropical sea fish.

clue.text: Temperamental rodent keeps swishing tail

indicators.note: keeps means the rodent holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent

indicators.note: a tail swishing about moves its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A moody little animal flicks its tail about irritably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swishing' makes ATIL from the tail, and 'keeps' sets it inside the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile describes a mood liable to change suddenly, much like an unpredictable temper.

clue.text: No gang of gunmen handled machine

definitions.meaning: not a gang but just ..., a single gunman
a fruit machine worked by pulling a handle or arm

explanation.surface: No band of armed robbers worked the slot machine.
explanation.definitionFit: One-armed bandit is the nickname for a gambling slot machine operated by a lever.

clue.text: Take in maid dancing tango

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of maid jig about into a new order

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Invite in a housemaid who is dancing the tango.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, to take them in.

clue.text: Admirer cheers to support popular princess

indicators.note: in a down answer the following pieces sit under the first, supporting it

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a fan is an admirer
ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A fan says thanks for backing a well-liked princess.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king, a princess.

clue.text: Checked rising water level — dredge in middle

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the tide is the rise and fall of the sea's level

indicators.note: in middle says take only the central letters of dredge

explanation.surface: A rising tide gets the riverbed dredged in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has been checked and corrected.

clue.text: Man's excellent knowledge about bad weather in border region

parts.note: Al's: Al is a man's name, with the possessive
ace means excellent

indicators.note: about means the knowledge goes around the weather

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A man's great know-how about storms in frontier country.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace-Lorraine is the territory on the French-German border that changed hands between the two countries.

clue.text: Agent good for Bond smashing luge into pieces

parts.note: smashing in the sense of excellent means super

indicators.note: a luge broken into pieces has its letters reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A secret agent fit for James Bond wrecks a toboggan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' and 'Bond' suggest spies, but bond here is a joint, and the agent is an adhesive. 'into pieces' turns LUGE into GLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Superglue is a strong adhesive, a bonding agent that sticks things together.

clue.text: Religious official sends note round university daily

indicators.note: round means the note goes about the other letters

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A cleric circulates a memo around a university every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is a Muslim legal scholar who issues rulings on Islamic law.

clue.text: North country area includes very serene place

indicators.note: includes means the country holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A tranquil spot found in the northern region of some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect peace, loosely any blissful, tranquil haven.

clue.text: Royal attendants bemoan banking eastern money

indicators.note: banking means putting away safely, so these letters are held inside the verb

parts.note: to rue something is to regret or bemoan it
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Courtiers complain while depositing foreign cash at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of aides and servants accompanying an important person, such as a monarch.

clue.text: Miserable husband initially under one choosing austerity

parts.note: miserable means sad

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word under

explanation.surface: A gloomy husband living beneath someone who has opted for frugality.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man who renounces worldly comforts for an ascetic life.

clue.text: Former barrister maybe killing time sees model

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: killing a letter means taking it out of the word

parts.note: a Templar is a lawyer of the Inner or Middle Temple in London, so maybe a barrister

explanation.surface: An ex-lawyer who once killed time now looks at a role model.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner and Middle Temple are two of London's Inns of Court, where barristers train.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect example to be copied, which is what a model is.

clue.text: Clerk one to provide assistance in swan-upping?

definitions.meaning: a dismissive name for an office clerk

definitions.text: one to provide assistance in swan-upping?
definitions.meaning: a pen is a female swan, so someone who pushes pens up would help at swan-upping

explanation.surface: A clerk is enlisted to help with the annual swan count.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan-upping is the yearly ceremony on the Thames in which swans are caught, marked and released.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is an office worker doing routine paperwork, a clerk.

clue.text: Lie with maid in spring, among forest creatures

indicators.note: among means one piece is put in the midst of the other

parts.note: deer are forest creatures
a spring is a flow of water

explanation.surface: A seduction in springtime, surrounded by woodland animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflower is to take a woman's virginity, so to lie with a maiden.

clue.text: Sacrifice and explosive combat at sea

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of combat are muddled

explanation.surface: Wartime losses and bombs as a naval battle rages.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was an ancient Greek offering of a hundred cattle, hence any large-scale sacrifice.

clue.text: Times getting letters from Greek theologian

parts.note: eras are long periods of time
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and mus are more than one of it

explanation.surface: The Times prints a Greek theologian's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' seems to describe the theologian, but it supplies the letters; Erasmus was Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance scholar and theologian behind a famous Greek New Testament.

clue.text: First book stolen from dope makes grand

indicators.note: stolen from means one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: to nobble a racehorse is to dope it

indicators.note: First says only the opening letter of the word book is the one stolen

explanation.surface: Taking a key volume from a junkie earns a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like slang for a thousand but is an adjective here; to nobble a racehorse is to drug it, and 'stolen from' takes one B out of NOBBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble and grand both describe something stately and impressive in appearance.

clue.text: Scolded, undergo assessment?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to be given a rating, so to be assessed

explanation.definitionFit: To berate someone is to scold or rebuke them sharply.

clue.text: Pirate's prop to fix on stage?

parts.note: to peg something is to fix it in place
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A pirate's prop to fix on stage, like a theatrical costume item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests theatre and 'prop' a stage prop, but the stage is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg leg is a wooden leg, the classic support of a storybook pirate.

clue.text: Entrance needs locks turned by soldiers without uniform

indicators.note: turned means the word for locks is read backwards

parts.note: a mane is a head of long hair, or locks

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the soldiers surround the letter

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A doorway with a curtain of hair, and troops out of uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway but is the verb to captivate; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate them, which is what enamour means.

clue.text: Mighty growth around Steppes originally a city

indicators.note: around means the tree goes round the next letter

parts.note: an oak grows mightily from a little acorn

indicators.note: originally says take only the first letter of Steppes

explanation.surface: A huge tree around the plains of Russia was once a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan.

clue.text: Renault changing gear

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters of the car's name

explanation.surface: A French car shifting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gearbox position in which no gear is engaged.

clue.text: Vampire, firstly impaled, interred by priest

indicators.note: interred by means buried inside the next piece

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

indicators.note: firstly says take only the opening letter of impaled

explanation.surface: A vampire is staked and then buried by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamia is a female monster of classical myth who sucked the blood of children, a vampire.

clue.text: Saint feeding cut flower before providing dish

indicators.note: before puts the flower ahead of the rest

parts.note: an iris is a flower

indicators.note: feeding means the saint is put into the cut

parts.note: to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A saint arranges cut flowers before serving dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut flower' tempts one to read a single idea, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'feeding' sets the saint inside the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a dish of mutton, potatoes and onions.

clue.text: Material from Web in plan approved to hold crowd back

indicators.note: to hold means the plan word keeps the other letters inside

parts.note: an approved plan is a goer, a scheme that will go ahead

indicators.note: back means the word for crowd is read in reverse

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

explanation.surface: Fabric found online is in a scheme that gets the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web' suggests the internet but is a spider's web. 'back' turns the crowd round to SSAM, which 'to hold' places inside the approved plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is the fine silken thread spun by spiders, the stuff of cobwebs.

clue.text: Ship on move suddenly reverses

indicators.note: reverses means the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
to dart is to move suddenly

explanation.surface: A vessel under way abruptly goes astern.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is a merchant vessel, a ship that carries goods for trade.
